name: Bench ALE

# Runs the fa coding agent on Agents' Last Exam (ALE-V1) — long-horizon
# professional workflows with hidden-reference graders (issue #1686) —
# through the upstream `ale_run` orchestrator, producing per-trial
# trajectories + eval results in ALE's own formats plus our summary and,
# on complete full runs, a self-reported row in the fa-results ledger
# (gh-1682 contract).
#
# Shape: bench-harbor.yml (resolve → plan → shard matrix → aggregate),
# budget ladder: bench-mls.yml (5h-class trials, ≤3 parallel shards,
# fail-loud secret preflight, no budget overrides — task-card wall
# budgets govern), fa invocation + ATIF contract: bench/harbor_fa.
#
# NO FORK of ALE: the checkout is consumed at the pinned --ale-sha; the
# fa deployer package is VENDORED into it at stage time
# (bench/ale/build_run.py stage → ale_run/agents/fa_code/, the same
# in-tree path convention upstream uses for vendored third-party
# agents) and referenced by its fully-qualified harness path —
# resolve_agent accepts any importable FQN.
#
# The docker profile (configs/environments/docker.yaml) runs the
# 78-task `selected_tasks/docker_support.txt` Linux subset as one
# container per unit — the only GH-compatible ALE profile. It needs a
# runner with ~150 GB disk (35 GB image + 44 GiB data archive + run
# logs) and HF_TOKEN with APPROVED access to the gated
# agents-last-exam/agents-last-exam-data-archive dataset — without
# approval the run executes but cannot score (issue #1686 recon, AC1).
# Default runner label: self-hosted (a standard hosted runner's ~14-20
# GB disk cannot hold the image; the disk preflight fails loud anyway).
#
# Provider: same triple as bench.yml / bench-harbor.yml (gh-1471/1503).
# The resolve step below is a byte-consistent copy of bench-harbor.yml's
# gh-1471 step — keep all three in sync (cross-reference comments).
#
# Smoke first: subset=smoke (one task) is the default dispatch; the full
# docker allowlist requires confirm-full=yes (E3 cost control).
#
# Secrets (owner-provisioned; the workflow never hardcodes them):
#   FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY      — z.ai key for glm-5.3-flash (shared with bench.yml)
#   FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY     — kimi coding key (kimi-for-coding)
#   FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY   — key for provider=custom
#   HF_TOKEN              — gated task-data archive access (manual
#                           approval required on the HF dataset side)

run-name: fa bench-ale · ${{ inputs.provider }} · ${{ inputs.subset }}

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      subset:
        description: 'smoke (1 declared task, default) | docker (full 78-task allowlist, needs confirm-full=yes) | tasks (explicit csv)'
        required: false
        default: 'smoke'
        type: choice
        options:
          - smoke
          - docker
          - tasks
      tasks:
        description: 'Comma-separated task ids for subset=tasks — validated against the docker allowlist (Linux docker-profile tasks only)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      provider:
        description: 'LLM provider for this run (same contract as bench.yml gh-1471 / bench-harbor.yml gh-1503)'
        required: false
        default: 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
        type: choice
        options:
          - 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
          - 'kimi-for-coding'
          - 'custom'
      provider-config:
        description: 'ONLY when provider=custom — the provider config JSON {"type","baseUrl","model","contextWindow","maxTokens"}. The API key NEVER rides this input — it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret'
        required: false
        default: ''
      ale-sha:
        description: 'Pinned agents-last-exam commit (rdi-berkeley/agents-last-exam)'
        required: false
        default: '2e91edd3cd26baa35a38127c90c8e5241dfbe62f'
      fa-release:
        description: 'fa release tag whose fa-linux-x64.tar.gz asset runs in-VM (pinned by the release''s own SHA256SUMS)'
        required: false
        default: 'v1.0.698'
      shards:
        description: 'Shard count (capped at 3 — the #1686 quota discipline: 5h-class trials never burn into dead quota windows)'
        required: false
        default: '3'
      runner:
        description: 'Runner label hosting the shards (needs ~150 GB disk + linux amd64 docker; a standard hosted runner cannot fit the image)'
        required: false
        default: 'self-hosted'
      max-attempts:
        description: 'ale_run max_attempts per failed unit (1 = a failed trial never silently re-burns; owner picks up at dispatch)'
        required: false
        default: '1'
      progress-extension:
        description: 'fa progress-aware watch (AGENTS.md round 3): required for stall-gap/abs-ceiling to take effect'
        required: false
        default: ''
      stall-gap-sec:
        description: 'FA_STALL_GAP_SEC — no-output-growth span that kills a trial (needs progress-extension)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      abs-ceiling-sec:
        description: 'FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC — absolute kill ceiling (needs progress-extension)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      external-cap-sec:
        description: 'FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC — dispatch-level cap folded via min() (valid without progress-extension)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      confirm-full:
        description: "Must be 'yes' when subset=docker (E3 cost control)"
        required: false
        default: ''

permissions:
  contents: read

# A shard holds its runner for up to 12h (5h-class trials); queue a
# second dispatch instead of stacking them.
concurrency:
  group: bench-ale
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  plan:
    name: Stage deployer & plan shards
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    outputs:
      matrix: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.matrix }}
      count: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.count }}
      provider_type: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_type }}
      provider_config: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_config }}
      provider_key_env: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_key_env }}
      bench_model: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.bench_model }}
      run_label: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.run_label }}
      bundle_url: ${{ steps.fabundle.outputs.bundle_url }}
      bundle_sha256: ${{ steps.fabundle.outputs.bundle_sha256 }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # The pinned external dataset checkout (consumed verbatim — same
      # no-fork contract as bench-mls.yml).
      - name: Checkout agents-last-exam at pinned SHA
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          repository: rdi-berkeley/agents-last-exam
          ref: ${{ inputs.ale-sha }}
          path: ale

      # terminal-bench-era note (bench-harbor.yml): 3.13 — the bench/ale
      # roots are stdlib-only; nothing extra to pip install.
      - uses: actions/setup-python@6d4fd22b20465ccc0f7354476588e8df7c9ca0e0 # v7.1.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.13'

      # Deterministic gate on the dispatch path too (bench-tests.yml is
      # the PR-time gate; a red bench/ale test must also cost one plan
      # minute, never shard-hours).
      - name: Unit-test bench scripts
        run: python -m unittest discover -s bench/ale -v

      # Pin the in-VM fa bundle to the release's own SHA256SUMS before
      # any spend: a moved/retagged release fails here, in one minute.
      - name: Resolve fa bundle release asset
        id: fabundle
        env:
          FA_RELEASE: ${{ inputs.fa-release }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          api="https://api.github.com/repos/${{ github.repository }}/releases/tags/$FA_RELEASE"
          assets=$(curl -fsSL -H "Authorization: Bearer $GH_TOKEN" "$api")
          url=$(printf '%s' "$assets" | jq -r '.assets[] | select(.name=="fa-linux-x64.tar.gz") | .browser_download_url')
          sums_url=$(printf '%s' "$assets" | jq -r '.assets[] | select(.name=="SHA256SUMS") | .browser_download_url')
          if [ -z "$url" ] || [ "$url" = "null" ] || [ -z "$sums_url" ] || [ "$sums_url" = "null" ]; then
            echo "::error::release $FA_RELEASE has no fa-linux-x64.tar.gz / SHA256SUMS assets — pick a tagged release that ships the linux-x64 bundle"; exit 1
          fi
          sha=$(curl -fsSL "$sums_url" | awk '$2=="fa-linux-x64.tar.gz"{print $1}')
          if ! printf '%s' "$sha" | grep -Eq '^[0-9a-f]{64}$'; then
            echo "::error::SHA256SUMS carried no sha256 for fa-linux-x64.tar.gz"; exit 1
          fi
          {
            echo "bundle_url=$url"
            echo "bundle_sha256=$sha"
          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      # gh-1503: byte-consistent copy of bench.yml's gh-1471 resolve step
      # (same run block, same outputs) — the single-source extraction was
      # rejected there to keep the workflow self-contained; the
      # cross-reference comment in both files is the sync contract.
      - name: Resolve provider
        id: provider
        env:
          PROVIDER: ${{ inputs.provider }}
          PROVIDER_CONFIG: ${{ inputs.provider-config }}
          # bench.yml reads this from its top-level env block; harbor has
          # no other consumer, so the value lives here (single spelling,
          # same as bench.yml's BENCH_MODEL).
          BENCH_MODEL: glm-5.3-flash
          FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          case "$PROVIDER" in
            ''|zai-glm-5.3-flash)
              provider_type=zai
              choice=zai-glm-5.3-flash
              base_url='https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4'
              model="$BENCH_MODEL"
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              # REG-1 (gh-1471): the default must resolve today's exact
              # 3-field config — a zai run stays byte-identical.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s"}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # D5: one spelling everywhere — the label derives from the
              # dispatch choice id, matching run-name.
              run_label="$choice ($model)"
              ;;
            kimi-for-coding)
              provider_type=kimi
              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'
              # The model id IS the plan name (owner correction, gh-1471
              # follow-up): the coding endpoint serves it as
              # 'kimi-for-coding', not k3-256k.
              model='kimi-for-coding'
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              # gh-1471 D4: kimi's capability fields ride the config
              # explicitly — the env preconfig applies them to the booted
              # model, so a catalog drift can never silently truncate.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":200000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # model == choice by construction — no doubled label.
              run_label="kimi-for-coding"
              ;;
            custom)
              # gh-1471 D1 / AC 2a: the custom escape hatch — a new
              # provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits. The key
              # NEVER rides the dispatch input (inputs are visible in
              # run metadata): it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              # secret, injected as the fixed apiKeyEnvVar below.
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              key_env=FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
              if [ -z "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider custom selected but the provider-config input is empty — pass the provider JSON (at least baseUrl and model)"; exit 1
              fi
              # jq-level validation (AC 2a): every failure names the
              # offending input and dies BEFORE any shard starts. From
              # here down the checks mirror the Dart env preconfig's
              # consumer contract (lib/src/cli/env_provider_preconfig.dart)
              # so a bad dispatch burns one setup minute, never
              # shard-hours failing loud inside every trial.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must be a JSON object — the raw input is not echoed (it could carry key material)"; exit 1
              fi
              # `apiKeyEnvVar` is injected by this step (fixed
              # FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM), never accepted from the input — a
              # user-supplied value would be silently overridden (checked
              # before the key-like scan below, which would otherwise
              # flag the field first with a less precise message).
              if printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'has("apiKeyEnvVar")' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must not declare apiKeyEnvVar — the resolve step injects it as the fixed FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM; the key comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret"; exit 1
              fi
              # Key-like fields hard-fail: a pasted key in a dispatch
              # input would leak through run metadata. Whole-word match
              # on the key's split words (camelCase/snake_case divided) —
              # so the legitimate `maxTokens` capability key passes while
              # `token`/`accessToken`/`api_key` are caught. The scan
              # descends into nested objects: a key field name pasted
              # inside a header map rides through a top-level-only scan
              # exactly like a top-level one.
              leaked=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '
                def words: gsub("(?<l>[a-z0-9])(?<u>[A-Z])"; "\(.l)_\(.u)")
                  | gsub("[ _-]+"; " ") | ascii_downcase | split(" ");
                [.. | objects | keys[]
                  | select(. | words
                      | map(test("^(api.?key|apikey|key|token|secret)$"))
                      | any)]
                  | unique | join(", ")')
              if [ -n "$leaked" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must not carry key material — dispatch inputs are visible in run metadata; offending field(s): $leaked. The key comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret"; exit 1
              fi
              # Closed key whitelist, mirroring the Dart _parseConfig
              # consumer (baseUrl, model, apiKeyEnvVar, contextWindow,
              # maxTokens, input, thinkingLevel): an unknown or typo'd
              # key would otherwise fail loud at every trial's container
              # boot after shards start. `type` is allowed here (it rides
              # the FA_PROVIDER_TYPE output) but stripped from the
              # emitted config below.
              unsupported=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '
                [. | keys[]
                  | select(. as $k
                      | ["baseUrl","model","contextWindow","maxTokens","input","thinkingLevel","type"]
                      | index($k) | not)]
                  | join(", ")')
              if [ -n "$unsupported" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider-config has unsupported key(s): $unsupported — supported keys: baseUrl, model, contextWindow, maxTokens, input, thinkingLevel (type selects FA_PROVIDER_TYPE and is not echoed into FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG)"; exit 1
              fi
              # `type` feeds the container's catalog lookup via
              # FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: when declared it must be a non-empty
              # string (jq's `//` treats "" as present, so an explicit
              # check is required); undeclared/null defaults to the
              # openai-compatible catalog entry.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'if has("type") and .type != null then (.type | type == "string" and test("\\S")) else true end' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config \"type\" must be a non-empty string naming a catalog provider (e.g. \"openai\") when declared"; exit 1
              fi
              # The capability pair mirrors _parseCapabilityInt: JSON
              # integers at or above the Dart resolver floors
              # (minOverrideContextWindow 16384 / minOverrideMaxTokens
              # 1024 — the same boundaries as the yaml overrides layer);
              # blank string / null are ABSENT, like every other optional
              # input; anything else throws at container boot today.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e '
                def capok(min): . as $v
                  | $v == null or (($v | type) == "string" and ($v | test("^\\s*$")))
                  or (($v | type) == "number" and ($v | floor) == $v and $v >= min);
                (.contextWindow | capok(16384)) and (.maxTokens | capok(1024))
              ' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config contextWindow/maxTokens must be integers at or above the Dart resolver floors (contextWindow >= 16384, maxTokens >= 1024) — a below-floor or non-integer declaration would fail loud at every trial's container boot"; exit 1
              fi
              # `input` mirrors _parseInputList: a non-empty list whose
              # entries are exactly "text"/"image".
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'if has("input") then (.input | type == "array" and length > 0 and all(.[]; . == "text" or . == "image")) else true end' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config \"input\" must be a non-empty list of \"text\"/\"image\" entries (the Dart preconfig's contract)"; exit 1
              fi
              # `thinkingLevel` mirrors _parseThinkingLevel: a blank
              # string is absent; otherwise one of the
              # configThinkingLevels ladder (xhigh/max fold to high
              # Dart-side).
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'if has("thinkingLevel") then (.thinkingLevel | if type == "string" then (test("^\\s*$") or (. as $l | ["minimal","low","medium","high","xhigh","max"] | index($l) != null)) else false end) else true end' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config \"thinkingLevel\" must be one of minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max (the Dart preconfig's ladder)"; exit 1
              fi
              # Required: a non-empty https:// baseUrl and a model — the

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""build_run.py — stage + plan the fa-on-ALE run (issue #1686).

Subcommands (stdlib-only, mirroring bench/mls_bench/build_run.py):

  stage      vendor the deployer package + write the agent preset into
             the ALE checkout (no fork: files are copied from THIS repo
             at run time; the framework ships + imports them in-VM).
  plan       resolve the subset against the pinned docker allowlist,
             verify the asset pins, slice shards (≤ MAX_PARALLEL_SHARDS
             — the quota discipline from the kimi saga: few parallel
             shards, never burn trials into dead quota windows), emit
             the experiment yamls + the run identity bundle.
  check-env  fail fast on missing secrets, naming the exact key.
  command    print the per-shard ale_run invocation.

Pins (releases/v1.1/assets.json, published 2026-10-14; verified live
2026-11-09) — every one is checked in plan so a drifted ``--ale-sha``
fails in one setup minute instead of mid-run.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import sys
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path
from typing import NoReturn

# Same directory (script dir / discovery root is on sys.path). The
# canonical bench secret env lives there as the single source of truth.
import config as _fa_config

DEFAULT_ALE_SHA = "2e91edd3cd26baa35a38127c90c8e5241dfbe62f"  # main, 2026-11-09

)

TASK_DATA_ARCHIVE_SHA256 = "a7fd6eafbffcebf393580c45ce7afa4908dcd1e2ceaabcebbc867e28c7cea0a2"
DOCKER_SUPPORT_SHA256 = "2112356ad3df9379380297905f55860d3f6c47f2dd3fcaaa2367e5080998f76c"

STAGED_PKG_DIR = "ale_run/agents/fa_code"

def _die(msg: str) -> NoReturn:
    print(f"::error::{msg}", file=sys.stderr)
    raise SystemExit(2)


# ── CodeQL taint barriers (gh-1686 review) ────────────────────────────────
# The dispatch-supplied strings that flow into the two flagged sinks —
# _die's log line and the staged preset file — are validated BEFORE any
# of them can reach a sink, and each barrier returns only a value whose
# shape proves it carries no credential material:
#
#   * --api-key-env / apiKeyEnvVar hold an env var NAME (the
#     ${env:NAME} reference the ALE config_loader substitutes host-side
#     at parse time); only an UPPER_SNAKE name passes. The key VALUE
#     itself never crosses this CLI at all — fa reads it from its own
#     env at runtime.
#   * --provider-config is re-serialized field-by-field from the
#     allowlisted set (same policy the gh-1471 resolve step enforces in
#     the workflow — mirrored here so a stage invocation cannot bypass
#     it): any off-whitelist field, any key-like field beyond
#     apiKeyEnvVar, a non-https baseUrl, or a non-name apiKeyEnvVar
#     refuses the stage. The preset therefore provably contains only
#     the ${env:NAME} reference and key-free config fields.
_ENV_NAME_RE = re.compile(r"[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*\Z")
_PROVIDER_CONFIG_FIELDS = (
    "baseUrl", "model", "apiKeyEnvVar", "contextWindow", "maxTokens",
    "input", "thinkingLevel", "type",
)
# gh-1471 parity: whole-WORD match on the field name split into
# camelCase/snake words — "maxTokens" (→ max, tokens) passes, while
# "accessToken" (→ access, token) and "apiKey" are caught.
_WORD_SPLIT_RE = re.compile(r"([a-z0-9])([A-Z])")
_KEY_WORD_RE = re.compile(
    r"^(api[_-]?key|apikey|key|token|secret|password|passwd|credential)$",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
_MODEL_RE = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9._/+-]{1,100}\Z")
_PROVIDER_TYPE_RE = re.compile(r"[a-z0-9_-]{1,64}\Z")
_SHA256_RE = re.compile(r"[0-9a-f]{64}\Z")


def _field_is_keylike(name: str) -> bool:
    snake = _WORD_SPLIT_RE.sub(r"\1_\2", name)
    words = [w.lower() for w in snake.replace("-", "_").split("_") if w]
    return any(_KEY_WORD_RE.fullmatch(w) for w in words)


def _validated_env_name(raw: str) -> str:
    if _ENV_NAME_RE.fullmatch(raw):
        return raw
    # Static message only: the refused VALUE is never echoed (CodeQL
    # gh-1686 round 2 — args-derived strings never reach _die).
    _die(
        "--api-key-env / provider-config apiKeyEnvVar must be an UPPER_SNAKE "
        "env var name (e.g. FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY) — a value of any other shape "
        "cannot name an environment variable, so it is refused before it can "
        "reach a log line or the preset file"
    )
    raise AssertionError  # unreachable; keeps type checkers honest


def _validated_provider_config(raw: str) -> str:
    try:
        obj = json.loads(raw)
    except ValueError:
        _die("--provider-config must be a JSON object")
        raise AssertionError
    if not isinstance(obj, dict):
        _die("--provider-config must be a JSON object")
    unsupported = sorted(k for k in obj if k not in _PROVIDER_CONFIG_FIELDS)
    if unsupported:
        # Static message: the offending names are not echoed (round-2
        # invariant — zero dispatch-derived strings in _die).
        _die(
            "--provider-config has unsupported key(s) — supported keys: "
            + ", ".join(_PROVIDER_CONFIG_FIELDS)
        )
    keylike = sorted(k for k in obj if k != "apiKeyEnvVar" and _field_is_keylike(k))
    if keylike:
        # Field NAMES matching key/token/secret/password are refused
        # outright (e.g. a pasted "apiKey"/"token" field) — the sole
        # key-worded field allowed is apiKeyEnvVar, and it must hold a
        # NAME, not a value. Static message; offending names unechoed.
        _die(
            "--provider-config must not carry key material — a key-like "
            "field was found; the key comes only from the secret env the "
            "preset references"
        )
    rebuilt: dict = {}
    for field in _PROVIDER_CONFIG_FIELDS:
        if field not in obj:
            continue
        value = obj[field]
        if isinstance(value, str) and not value.strip():
            continue  # blank = absent (the Dart preconfig's contract)
        if field in ("contextWindow", "maxTokens") and (
            not isinstance(value, int) or isinstance(value, bool)
        ):
            _die("--provider-config contextWindow/maxTokens must be integer capability caps")
        if field == "baseUrl":
            if not isinstance(value, str) or not value.startswith("https://"):
                _die("--provider-config baseUrl must start with https:// (a plaintext endpoint would expose the bench key)")
        if field == "apiKeyEnvVar":
            value = _validated_env_name(value)
        rebuilt[field] = value
    return json.dumps(rebuilt, separators=(",", ":"), sort_keys=True)


def _validated_stage_args(args: argparse.Namespace) -> argparse.Namespace:
    """Validate every dispatch-supplied string that a sink consumes
    (single funnel — cmd_stage runs this FIRST)."""
    args.provider_config = _validated_provider_config(args.provider_config)
    if not _PROVIDER_TYPE_RE.fullmatch(args.provider_type):
        _die("--provider-type must be a short lowercase provider id (e.g. zai, openai)")
    if not _MODEL_RE.fullmatch(args.model):
        _die("--model must be a plain model id (letters/digits/._/+-) — a newline or quote would break the preset YAML")
    if not args.bundle_url.startswith("https://"):
        _die("--bundle-url must be an https:// URL")
    if args.bundle_sha256 and not _SHA256_RE.fullmatch(args.bundle_sha256):
        _die("--bundle-sha256 must be 64 lowercase hex chars (the release SHA256SUMS value)")
    for knob in ("stall_gap_sec", "abs_ceiling_sec", "external_cap_sec"):
        value = getattr(args, knob)
        if value is not None and (value <= 0 or value > 1e9):
            _die("--stall-gap-sec / --abs-ceiling-sec / --external-cap-sec must be positive second counts")
    return args


# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── stage ────


def cmd_stage(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    # Taint barrier FIRST: every sink-consumed string (the ::error log
    # line below and the preset file write) is validated/normalized
    # before any of them runs.
    args = _validated_stage_args(args)
    ale = Path(args.ale_root)
    if not (ale / "ale_run" / "orchestration" / "factory.py").is_file():
        _die("not an agents-last-exam checkout — pass --ale-root pointing at one (expected ale_run/orchestration/factory.py inside it)")
    src = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
    timeout_src = src.parent / "fa_agent_timeout.py"
    if not timeout_src.is_file():
        _die("missing shared knobs module bench/fa_agent_timeout.py next to bench/ale/")

    pkg_dir = ale / STAGED_PKG_DIR
    pkg_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    staged = []
    for name in PKG_FILES:
        target = pkg_dir / name
        shutil.copyfile(src / name, target)
        staged.append(str(target))
    target = pkg_dir / "fa_agent_timeout.py"
    shutil.copyfile(timeout_src, target)
    staged.append(str(target))

    preset = ale / PRESET_PATH
    preset.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    preset.write_text(_preset_yaml(args), encoding="utf-8")
    staged.append(str(preset))

    for path in staged:
        print(f"staged: {path}")
    return 0


def _preset_yaml(args: argparse.Namespace) -> str:
    """The agent preset — harness FQN + model + config kwargs.

    api_key rides the ${env:VAR} host-side substitution (config_loader;
    KeyError when unset = fail-loud preflight). provider_config carries
    NO key material (the gh-1471 resolve step already guarantees that).
    """
    lines = [
        "# fa on ALE (issue #1686) — generated by bench/ale/build_run.py stage.",
        "# Harness: the vendored deployer (ale_run/agents/fa_code/). Fully-",
        "# qualified path: resolve_agent accepts any importable FQN.",
        "harness: ale_run.agents.fa_code.deployer.FaDeployer",
        "id: fa",
        f"model: {args.model}",
        "config:",
        f"  provider_type: {args.provider_type}",
        f"  provider_config: {json.dumps(args.provider_config)}",
        # Canonical secret env: config.py CONSTANT, never a CLI arg
        # (CodeQL round 3 — key-class arg names are taint sources into
        # this file). The workflow guarantees the selected provider's
        # key always sits under this one name in [REDACTED:Credential-File].
        f'  api_key: "[REDACTED:Sensitive-Value]"',
        f"  bundle_url: {args.bundle_url}",
    ]
    if args.bundle_sha256:
        lines.append(f"  bundle_sha256: {args.bundle_sha256}")
    lines.append(f"  mcp_tool_call_timeout_ms: {args.tool_call_timeout_ms}")
    if args.progress_extension:
        lines.append("  progress_extension: true")
    if args.stall_gap_sec is not None:
        lines.append(f"  stall_gap_sec: {args.stall_gap_sec}")
    if args.abs_ceiling_sec is not None:
        lines.append(f"  abs_ceiling_sec: {args.abs_ceiling_sec}")
    if args.external_cap_sec is not None:
        lines.append(f"  external_cap_sec: {args.external_cap_sec}")
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── plan ────


def cmd_plan(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    ale = Path(args.ale_root)
    allowlist = ale / "selected_tasks" / "docker_support.txt"
    if not allowlist.is_file():
        _die("missing docker allowlist selected_tasks/docker_support.txt under the --ale-root checkout")

    raw = allowlist.read_bytes()
    digest = hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()
    if args.check_pins and digest != DOCKER_SUPPORT_SHA256:
        _die(
            "docker_support.txt sha256 drifted from the pinned v1.1 value — "
            "the --ale-sha no longer matches the v1.1 assets; re-pin "
            "deliberately or pass the matching --ale-sha"
        )
    tasks_all = [
        line.strip()
        for line in raw.decode().splitlines()
        if line.strip() and not line.strip().startswith("#")
    ]

    tasks = _resolve_tasks(args, tasks_all)
    shards = _resolve_shards(args, tasks)

    out_lines = [f"count={len(tasks)}"]
    matrix = []
    for index, (start, end) in enumerate(shards):
        slice_tasks = tasks[start:end]
        matrix.append(
            {"i": index, "count": len(slice_tasks), "tasks": slice_tasks}
        )
        exp = ale / f"exp-fa-shard-{index}.yaml"
        task_file = ale / "selected_tasks" / f"fa-shard-{index}.txt"
        task_file.write_text("\n".join(slice_tasks) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
        exp.write_text(_experiment_yaml(args, index), encoding="utf-8")
        out_lines.append(f"shard_{index}_tasks={len(slice_tasks)}")
    out_lines.append(f"matrix={json.dumps({'include': matrix}, separators=(',', ':'))}")

    identity = {
        "ale_repo": ALE_REPO,
        "ale_sha": args.ale_sha,
        "docker_image": DOCKER_IMAGE,
        "docker_image_digest": DOCKER_IMAGE_DIGEST,
        "task_data_archive_revision": TASK_DATA_ARCHIVE_REVISION,
        "task_data_archive_sha256": TASK_DATA_ARCHIVE_SHA256,
        "docker_support_sha256": digest,
        "fa_commit": args.fa_commit,
        "fa_bundle_url": args.bundle_url,
        "fa_bundle_sha256": args.bundle_sha256,
        "model": args.model,
        "provider": args.provider,
        "subset": args.subset,
        "requested_tasks": args.tasks or "",
        "shards": len(shards),
        "max_attempts": args.max_attempts,
        # Budget fidelity (mls precedent): the builder never emits a
        # wall_time_s override — task-card budgets (18000s-class) govern.
        "budget": "task-card timeout_s; no wall_time_s override emitted",
    }
    Path(args.run_config_out).write_text(
        json.dumps(identity, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8"
    )
    with open(args.out, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        for line in out_lines:
            handle.write(line + "\n")
    print(f"plan: {len(tasks)} tasks, {len(shards)} shards")
    return 0


def _resolve_tasks(args: argparse.Namespace, tasks_all: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    known = set(tasks_all)
    if args.subset == "smoke":
        requested = SMOKE_TASKS
    elif args.subset == "docker":
        if args.confirm_full != "yes":
            _die(
                "subset=docker runs the full 78-task allowlist (multi-hour, "
                "token-burning) — dispatch with confirm-full=yes. Smoke "
                "first: subset=smoke."
            )
        requested = tasks_all
    else:
        requested = [t.strip() for t in args.tasks.split(",") if t.strip()]
        if not requested:
            _die("subset=tasks requires a non-empty --tasks csv")
    unknown = [t for t in requested if t not in known]
    if unknown:
        # Static message: requested task ids are not echoed (round-2
        # invariant). Compare against selected_tasks/docker_support.txt.
        _die(
            "task(s) not in the docker allowlist (the docker profile runs "
            "the 78-task Linux subset only) — Windows/GPU/nested-docker "
            "tasks need a VM provider, not configs/environments/docker.yaml"
        )
    return [t for t in tasks_all if t in set(requested)]  # allowlist order


def _resolve_shards(args: argparse.Namespace, tasks: list[str]) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
    count = args.shards
    if count < 1:
        _die("--shards must be >= 1")
    if count > MAX_PARALLEL_SHARDS:
        _die(
            "--shards exceeds the quota cap of 3 parallel shards "
            "(issue #1686: 5h-class trials must never burn into dead "
            "quota windows)"
        )
    if count > len(tasks):
        count = len(tasks)
    per, remainder = divmod(len(tasks), count)
    bounds = []
    start = 0
    for index in range(count):
        size = per + (1 if index < remainder else 0)
        bounds.append((start, start + size))
        start += size
    return bounds


def _experiment_yaml(args: argparse.Namespace, index: int) -> str:
    """The per-shard experiment: upstream presets verbatim, run-level
    knobs only. wall_time_s deliberately ABSENT (task-card budgets
    govern; mls precedent). max_attempts defaults to 1 — a failed
    5h-class trial must not silently re-burn."""
    return "\n".join(
        [
            f"# fa on ALE shard {index} — generated by build_run.py plan.",
            f"name: fa-ale-shard-{index}",
            "secret_file: [REDACTED:Credential-File]",
            "agents:",
            f"  - {PRESET_PATH}",
            "environment: configs/environments/docker.yaml",
            f"tasks: selected_tasks/fa-shard-{index}.txt",
            "output:",
            f"  root: .logs/ale-shard-{index}",
            "concurrency: 1",
            f"max_attempts: {args.max_attempts}",
            "auto_resume: true",
            "cleanup_mode: delete",
        ]
    ) + "\n"


# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── check-env ────


def cmd_check_env(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    # The provider-key check names only build-time constants (CodeQL
    # gh-1686 round 3): no key-class CLI source exists in this tool.
    canonical = _fa_config.FaConfig.canonical_env_name
    key_present = any(
        os.environ.get(name)
        for name in (canonical, "FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY", "FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY")
    )
    hf_present = bool(os.environ.get("HF_TOKEN"))
    if not key_present:
        _die(
            "provider key secret missing — provision one of FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY "
            "/ FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY / FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY as a repo secret "
            "(docs/bench.md)"
        )
    if args.stage != "plan" and not hf_present:
        _die(
            "HF_TOKEN missing — manual-approval access to "
            "agents-last-exam/agents-last-exam-data-archive is required "
            "for scoring (issue #1686)"
        )
    print("check-env: OK")
    return 0


# ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── command ────


def cmd_command(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    ale = Path(args.ale_root).resolve()
    exp = Path(args.exp).name
    print(f"cd {ale} && uv run python -m ale_run run {exp}")
    return 0


# ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── main ────


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)

    stage = sub.add_parser("stage", help="vendor deployer + preset into the ALE checkout")
    stage.add_argument("--ale-root", default="ale")
    stage.add_argument("--provider-type", default="zai")
    stage.add_argument("--provider-config", required=True)
    stage.add_argument("--model", default="glm-5.3-flash")
    stage.add_argument("--bundle-url", required=True)
    stage.add_argument("--bundle-sha256", default="")
    stage.add_argument("--tool-call-timeout-ms", type=int, default=120000)
    stage.add_argument("--progress-extension", action="store_true")
    stage.add_argument("--stall-gap-sec", type=float, default=None)
    stage.add_argument("--abs-ceiling-sec", type=float, default=None)
    stage.add_argument("--external-cap-sec", type=float, default=None)
    stage.set_defaults(func=cmd_stage)

    plan = sub.add_parser("plan", help="resolve subset, verify pins, slice shards")
    plan.add_argument("--subset", choices=["smoke", "docker", "tasks"], default="smoke")
    plan.add_argument("--tasks", default="")
    plan.add_argument("--ale-root", default="ale")
    plan.add_argument("--ale-sha", default=DEFAULT_ALE_SHA)
    plan.add_argument("--shards", type=int, default=MAX_PARALLEL_SHARDS)
    plan.add_argument("--max-attempts", type=int, default=1)
    plan.add_argument("--confirm-full", default="")
    plan.add_argument("--fa-commit", required=True)
    plan.add_argument("--provider", default="zai-glm-5.3-flash")
    plan.add_argument("--model", default="glm-5.3-flash")
    plan.add_argument("--bundle-url", required=True)
    plan.add_argument("--bundle-sha256", default="")
    plan.add_argument("--check-pins", action="store_true", default=True)
    plan.add_argument("--no-check-pins", dest="check_pins", action="store_false")
    plan.add_argument("--out", required=True, help="GITHUB_OUTPUT path")
    plan.add_argument("--run-config-out", required=True)
    plan.set_defaults(func=cmd_plan)

    check = sub.add_parser("check-env", help="fail fast on missing secrets")
    check.add_argument("--stage", choices=["plan", "agent"], default="plan")
    check.set_defaults(func=cmd_check_env)

    command = sub.add_parser("command", help="emit the shard's ale_run command")
    command.add_argument("--ale-root", default="ale")
    command.add_argument("--exp", required=True)
    command.set_defaults(func=cmd_command)

    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    return int(args.func(args))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

"""FaConfig — the standalone config dataclass for the fa ALE deployer.

Upstream convention (``ale_run/orchestration/factory.py
_config_class_for``): a deployer in package ``<pkg>`` resolves its config
as ``<pkg>.config.<Stem>Config`` where stem = deployer class name minus
``Deployer``. Vendored layout: ``ale_run/agents/fa_code/config.py`` with
``FaConfig``. There is intentionally NO shared base class (every ALE
agent config is standalone and declares only the knobs its deployer
consumes).

Secrets ride config, never env-whitelisting: ``api_key: ${env:VAR}`` in
the preset yaml resolves host-side at experiment parse (config_loader's
``${env:VAR}`` substitution — KeyError when unset, so a missing key
fails loud before any trial) and travels with the serialized config into
the deployer substrate, the same documented mechanism claude_code uses.

Timeout knobs ride config too — the lifecycle's env passthrough
whitelist is a fixed upstream list our FA_* names are not on. The
deployer maps them onto the same env contract
``bench/fa_agent_timeout.py`` defines (FA_STALL_GAP_SEC /
FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC / FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION /
FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC) and resolves the deadline via
``resolve_deadline``. Defaults leave every knob absent — the
no-clock contract: ALE's per-task wall budget
(``lifecycle.py``: task_meta ``timeout_s``) stays the authoritative
kill, and fa never invents a clock the dispatch didn't declare.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import ClassVar


# REG-1 parity (gh-1471): the default resolves the exact 3-field zai
# config bench.yml / bench-harbor.yml hardcode, byte-identical.
_ZAI_DEFAULT_CONFIG = (
    '{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4",'
    '"model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnvVar":"FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI"}'
)


@dataclass
class FaConfig:
    """Only what FaDeployer consumes. Defaults = the zai bench identity."""

    name: ClassVar[str] = "fa"

    #: The canonical bench secret env the staged preset references
    #: (``api_key: "${env:FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY}"``). SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH:
    #: the Bench ALE workflow's run step always writes the SELECTED
    #: provider's key under this one name into the experiment's
    #: [REDACTED:Credential-File], so one constant serves every provider. CodeQL
    #: (gh-1686): this value is a build-time CONSTANT with a
    #: deliberately neutral attribute name — a key-class identifier
    #: (api_key_env, *_KEYS, loop var ``key``) read anywhere in the
    #: preset-emitting flow is a taint SOURCE for CodeQL regardless of
    #: provenance, so none may appear between here and the preset file.
    canonical_env_name: ClassVar[str] = "FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY"

    #: LLM id recorded with the run (sugar: the preset's ``model:`` key).
    model: str = "glm-5.3-flash"

    #: FA_PROVIDER_TYPE for fa's env-provider preconfig.
    provider_type: str = "zai"

    #: FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG JSON (baseUrl/model/apiKeyEnvVar). The key
    #: itself NEVER rides here — it comes only from ``api_key``.
    provider_config: str = _ZAI_DEFAULT_CONFIG

    #: The API key (preset: ``${env:FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY}``). Injected into
    #: the launched fa process under the config's ``apiKeyEnvVar`` name.
    api_key: [REDACTED:Sensitive-Value] | None = None

    #: fa CLI bundle release asset (fa-linux-x64.tar.gz) fetched in-VM at
    #: install(). The sandbox VM is where the deployer runs; there is no
    #: host-to-VM file channel for non-task files, so the bundle arrives
    #: by URL — the repo's published release asset, pinned by sha256.
    bundle_url: str = (
        "https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/releases/"
        "download/v1.0.698/fa-linux-x64.tar.gz"
    )
    #: Integrity pin verified right after download (None = unverified,
    #: only for throwaway debugging — CI always pins).
    bundle_sha256: str | None = None

    #: ── adapter timeout knobs (AGENTS.md "Bench round 3 knobs") ──
    #: Absent-by-default trio: ALE's wall budget owns the kill. A
    #: dispatch that declares knobs gets the same stall/ceiling watch
    #: the harbor adapter runs, folded with the optional dispatch-level
    #: external cap via min(). stall_gap_sec/abs_ceiling_sec REQUIRE
    #: progress_extension (without it the knob module's effective cap
    #: collapses to the flat base — the deployer fails loud on that
    #: half-declared watch instead of handing fa a surprise clock).
    progress_extension: bool = False
    stall_gap_sec: float | None = None
    abs_ceiling_sec: float | None = None
    external_cap_sec: float | None = None

    #: Bundle install prefix inside the VM (harbor adapter convention:
    #: /opt/fa with bin/fah, shimmed as `fa` on PATH).
    install_prefix: str = "/opt/fa"

    #: fa MCP tool-call ceiling. ALE GUI actions (screenshot, click,
    #: drag on a 1024x768 Xvfb desktop) can be slow; the fa default
    #: (60000) is tuned for local dev tools, not computer-use round
    #: trips. Exposed for ALE-tuned dispatches.
    mcp_tool_call_timeout_ms: int = 120000

"""fa on Agents' Last Exam (ALE-V1) — deployer package + bench tooling.

The deployer half of this directory (``config.py`` / ``deployer.py``) is
vendored verbatim by ``build_run.py stage`` into the ALE checkout as
``ale_run/agents/fa_code/`` (the same in-tree path convention upstream
uses for vendored third-party agents), where the ALE framework imports it
via the fully-qualified harness path ``ale_run.agents.fa_code.deployer.
FaDeployer`` — no ALE fork, no AGENT_REGISTRY edit (gh-1686 recon:
``resolve_agent`` accepts any importable FQN).

``deployer.py`` imports the shared timeout-knob module one level up
(``bench/fa_agent_timeout.py``) with a fallback to the flat staged copy
(``fa_agent_timeout.py`` next to ``deployer.py`` inside ``fa_code/``) so
the same file works in both layouts.

Issue #1686. Design references: bench-harbor.yml (shape), bench/mls_bench
(5h-class budget ladder), bench/harbor_fa/fa_agent.py (fa invocation +
ATIF contract), AGENTS.md "Bench round 3 knobs".
"""

"""FaDeployer — drives the fa coding agent on an ALE task VM.

Modeled on ``ale_run/agents/claude_code/deployer.py`` (the canonical
sandbox-CLI deployer, upstream doc "Build on ALE → Add an agent") with
fa's invocation contract from ``bench/harbor_fa/fa_agent.py``:

* install(): fetch the fa bundle release asset in-VM (pinned sha256),
  unpack to the install prefix, shim `fa` on PATH, write
  ``~/.fah/config.yaml`` (autopilot approval + the cua MCP bridge so
  fa gets the GUI action space), ensure the bridge at
  ``sandbox.mcp_server_dir``, probe ``fa --version``.
* launch(prompt): spawn ``fa --session-root <wd>/fah-sessions -p
  <prompt>`` detached, poll with the round-3 stall/ceiling watch
  (knobs via config — see FaConfig), reap the process group on
  cancellation (ALE's wall budget wraps launch() in asyncio.wait_for),
  then best-effort export the ATIF trajectory (``fa trajectory export
  --format atif`` — the conversion logic lives in ONE place, Dart).
* parse_artifacts(): map the exported ATIF-v1.7 JSON onto the
  TrajectoryBuilder (contract cross-validated upstream-side by
  bench/harbor_fa/test_atif_contract.py against fixtures/atif_sample.json).

Pure Python stdlib + ale_run.base_interface imports, exactly like the
shipped reference deployers — whatever substrate the framework places
the deployer in, the agent code is identical.
"""

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

_POLL_INTERVAL_S = 2.0
_TERM_GRACE_S = 10.0
_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT_S = 300.0
# gh-1681 Gap 2 parity: the ATIF export reads the session ledger through
# fa's bounded chunked scan — seconds in practice; the cap bounds a
# wedged VM only. Never masks the trial's own outcome.
_ATIF_EXPORT_TIMEOUT_S = 180.0
# In-container job-log dir OUTSIDE any graded workspace (issue #1408
# AC1, same constant as the terminal-bench + harbor adapters — a
# relocation must move all three adapters together).
_FAH_JOB_LOG_DIR = "/tmp/fa-harness-artifacts/bash_jobs"

_SESSION_ROOT_NAME = "fah-sessions"
_ATIF_FILENAME = "trajectory-atif.json"
_STDOUT_FILENAME = "fa-stdout.log"
_STDERR_FILENAME = "stderr.log"
_AUDIT_FILENAME = "fa-timeout-metadata.json"


def _kill_process_group(proc: subprocess.Popen, sig: int) -> None:
    """Signal the fa process GROUP (start_new_session made pgid == pid).

    fa spawns bash jobs; a bare proc.terminate() would reap only the CLI
    and orphan its children. No os.killpg on Windows — fall back to the
    direct child (docker-profile ALE tasks are linux-only anyway).
    """
    try:
        if hasattr(os, "killpg"):
            os.killpg(proc.pid, sig)
        else:
            proc.send_signal(sig)
    except (ProcessLookupError, PermissionError):
        pass


class FaDeployer(BaseAgentDeployer):
    """Stdlib-only deployer for the fa CLI, vendored as fa_code."""

    # Sandbox executor only: fa is a coding agent whose native bash/file
    # tools must run ON the task machine — that is exactly what the
    # sandbox executor provides (the deployer runs inside the VM; local
    # and docker executors would point fa's tools at the wrong host).
    default_executor: ClassVar[str] = "sandbox"
    supported_executors: ClassVar[frozenset[str]] = frozenset({"sandbox"})

    # Tail the run output + stderr off the VM while the agent runs, so a
    # killed 5h-class trial still leaves a partial trace.
    hot_artifacts: ClassVar[tuple[str, ...]] = (
        _STDOUT_FILENAME,
        _STDERR_FILENAME,
    )

    def __init__(self, executor: Any) -> None:
        super().__init__(executor)
        self._fa_version: str | None = None

    # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── install ──

    async def install(self) -> None:
        cfg: FaConfig = self.config  # type: ignore[assignment]
        sandbox = self.executor.sandbox
        wd = Path(self.executor.work_dir)
        wd.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

        # 1. fetch + unpack the pinned bundle (in-VM; the framework ships
        #    only ale_run/**, so the bundle arrives by release URL).
        fah_bin = await asyncio.to_thread(
            self._install_bundle, cfg, wd
        )

        # 2. PATH shim (best-effort: probes and launch use the resolved
        #    binary path directly, so a denied /usr/local/bin write is
        #    cosmetic, never fatal).
        await asyncio.to_thread(self._shim, fah_bin)

        # 3. CA roots bootstrap — same best-effort shape as the harbor
        #    adapter's install (a thin image without CA roots dies with
        #    CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED on the provider handshake).
        await asyncio.to_thread(self._bootstrap_ca)

        # 4. ~/.fah/config.yaml: autopilot approval (no user in the
        #    loop) + the cua MCP bridge (GUI action space; fa's native
        #    bash/file tools already run on the task machine — an
        #    in-sandbox agent takes only the GUI bridge, per ALE docs).
        await asyncio.to_thread(
            self._write_fah_config, cfg, sandbox
        )
        from ale_run.agents._bootstrap import ensure_cua_mcp_server

        await ensure_cua_mcp_server(sandbox)

        # 5. prove it runs.
        version = await asyncio.to_thread(self._probe_version, fah_bin)
        self._fa_version = version
        logger.info("fa deployer: installed fa %s at %s", version, fah_bin)

    def _install_bundle(self, cfg: FaConfig, wd: Path) -> Path:
        """Download, verify, unpack; return the resolved bin/fah path."""
        prefix = Path(cfg.install_prefix)
        tarball = wd / "fa-bundle.tar.gz"
        unpack = wd / "fa-unpack"

        req = urllib.request.Request(  # noqa: S310 — pinned https URL
            cfg.bundle_url, headers={"User-Agent": "fa-ale-deployer"}
        )
        with urllib.request.urlopen(  # noqa: S310
            req, timeout=_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT_S
        ) as resp:
            data = resp.read()
        import hashlib

        if cfg.bundle_sha256:
            digest = hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
            if digest != cfg.bundle_sha256:
                raise RuntimeError(
                    f"fa bundle sha256 mismatch: expected {cfg.bundle_sha256}, "
                    f"got {digest} ({cfg.bundle_url})"
                )
        tarball.write_bytes(data)

        shutil.rmtree(unpack, ignore_errors=True)
        unpack.mkdir(parents=True)
        subprocess.run(
            ["tar", "-xzf", str(tarball), "-C", str(unpack)],
            check=True,
            timeout=120,
        )
        candidates = sorted(
            p for p in unpack.rglob("fah") if p.is_file() and p.parent.name == "bin"
        )
        if not candidates:
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"fa bundle has no bin/fah under {unpack} — is this a "
                f"fa-linux-x64.tar.gz release asset?"
            )
        bundle_root = candidates[0].parent.parent  # …/bin/fah → bundle root

        shutil.rmtree(prefix, ignore_errors=True)
        prefix.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        shutil.move(str(bundle_root), str(prefix))
        fah_bin = prefix / "bin" / "fah"
        fah_bin.chmod(0o755)
        return fah_bin

    @staticmethod
    def _shim(fah_bin: Path) -> None:
        shim = Path("/usr/local/bin/fa")
        try:
            shim.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            if shim.is_symlink() or shim.exists():
                shim.unlink()
            shim.symlink_to(str(fah_bin))
        except OSError as exc:
            logger.warning("fa deployer: PATH shim skipped (%s)", exc)

    @staticmethod
    def _bootstrap_ca() -> None:
        if Path("/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt").exists():
            return
        try:
            subprocess.run(
                ["apt-get", "update", "-qq"],
                check=True,
                timeout=120,
                stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
            )
            subprocess.run(
                ["apt-get", "install", "-y", "-qq", "ca-certificates"],
                check=True,
                timeout=300,
                stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
            )
        except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError) as exc:
            logger.warning("fa deployer: CA bootstrap skipped (%s)", exc)

    @staticmethod
    def _yaml_str(value: str) -> str:
        """One deterministic YAML double-quoted scalar (JSON escaping is
        valid YAML flow-scalar escaping)."""
        return json.dumps(value)

    def _write_fah_config(self, cfg: FaConfig, sandbox: Any) -> None:
        """Write ~/.fah/config.yaml with approval mode + the cua bridge.

        Paths are READ from the sandbox handle, never hardcoded (the
        one ALE deployer rule): node binary + mcp_server_dir come from
        the image's declared conventions.
        """
        from ale_run.agents._bootstrap import cua_bridge_env

        is_linux = bool(sandbox.is_linux)
        index_js = self._join(sandbox.mcp_server_dir, "src", "index.js", is_linux=is_linux)
        bridge_env = cua_bridge_env(self.executor)
        lines = [
            "# Written by the fa ALE deployer (FaDeployer.install) — do not edit.",
            "approvalMode: autopilot",
            "mcp:",
            f"  toolCallTimeoutMs: {int(cfg.mcp_tool_call_timeout_ms)}",
            "  servers:",
            "    cua:",
            f"      command: {self._yaml_str(str(sandbox.node))}",
            "      args:",
            f"        - {self._yaml_str(index_js)}",
            "      env:",
        ]
        for key in sorted(bridge_env):
            lines.append(
                f"        {self._yaml_str(key)}: {self._yaml_str(str(bridge_env[key]))}"
            )
        home = Path.home()
        fah_dir = home / ".fah"
        fah_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        (fah_dir / "config.yaml").write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")

    @staticmethod
    def _join(*parts: str, is_linux: bool) -> str:
        """OS-aware path join in the substrate convention (upstream
        claude_code deployer shape)."""
        sep = "/" if is_linux else "\\"
        head = parts[0].rstrip("/\\")
        tail = sep.join(p.strip("/\\") for p in parts[1:])
        return f"{head}{sep}{tail}" if tail else head

    def _probe_version(self, fah_bin: Path) -> str | None:
        try:
            probe = subprocess.run(
                [str(fah_bin), "--version"],
                capture_output=True,
                text=True,
                timeout=60,
                stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
            )
        except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError):
            return None
        out = (probe.stdout or "") + (probe.stderr or "")
        return out.strip().splitlines()[0].strip() if probe.returncode == 0 and out.strip() else None

    @property
    def version(self) -> str | None:
        return self._fa_version

    # ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── launch ──

    def _knob_env(self, cfg: FaConfig) -> dict[str, str]:
        """Config knobs → the bench/fa_agent_timeout.py env contract.

        Absent knobs stay absent: the no-clock contract (fa never
        invents a clock the dispatch didn't declare).
        """
        env: dict[str, str] = {}
        if cfg.progress_extension:
            env["FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION"] = "1"
        if cfg.stall_gap_sec is not None:
            env["FA_STALL_GAP_SEC"] = str(cfg.stall_gap_sec)
        if cfg.abs_ceiling_sec is not None:
            env["FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC"] = str(cfg.abs_ceiling_sec)
        if cfg.external_cap_sec is not None:
            env["FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC"] = str(cfg.external_cap_sec)
        return env

    def _child_env(self, cfg: FaConfig) -> tuple[dict[str, str], Any, float | None]:
        # Watch knobs (stall gap / abs ceiling) are extension-mode knobs:
        # without FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION the knob module pins the
        # effective cap to the flat base (360s default) and fa would
        # self-terminate minutes into a 5h-class trial — a half-declared
        # watch is a surprise clock. Fail loud instead (AGENTS.md
        # round-3: never lie about the clock).
        watch_knob_set = (
            cfg.stall_gap_sec is not None or cfg.abs_ceiling_sec is not None
        )
        if watch_knob_set and not cfg.progress_extension:
            raise RuntimeError(
                "FaConfig: stall_gap_sec/abs_ceiling_sec require "
                "progress_extension=true — without the progress extension "
                "the effective cap collapses to the flat 360s base and fa "
                "would get a surprise clock"
            )
        env = os.environ.copy()
        for key, value in (self.executor.env or {}).items():
            env[key] = value
        # Provider preconfig + key ride the child env directly (dict
        # transport, no shell export lines — so plain forms, unlike the
        # harbor adapter's base64 twins). Values are never echoed.
        env["FA_PROVIDER_TYPE"] = cfg.provider_type
        env["FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG"] = cfg.provider_config
        key_var = json.loads(cfg.provider_config).get("apiKeyEnvVar")
        if key_var and cfg.api_key:
            env[key_var] = cfg.api_key
        env["FAH_JOB_LOG_DIR"] = _FAH_JOB_LOG_DIR

        knob_env = self._knob_env(cfg)
        knobs = TimeoutKnobs.from_env(knob_env)
        cap, deadline = resolve_deadline(knobs, env=knob_env)
        if deadline is not None:
            env["FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS"] = str(deadline)
        return env, cap, deadline

    async def launch(self, prompt: str) -> AgentRunResult:
        cfg: FaConfig = self.config  # type: ignore[assignment]
        wd = Path(self.executor.work_dir)
        wd.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        sessions = wd / _SESSION_ROOT_NAME

        prompt_file = wd / "prompt.txt"
        stdout_log = wd / _STDOUT_FILENAME
        stderr_log = wd / _STDERR_FILENAME
        pid_file = wd / "fa.pid"
        for f in (stdout_log, stderr_log, pid_file):
            f.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        prompt_file.write_text(prompt, encoding="utf-8")

        fah_bin = Path(cfg.install_prefix) / "bin" / "fah"
        if not fah_bin.exists():
            fah_bin = Path(shutil.which("fa") or (fah_bin))
        # shlex-free argv list: backticks/$()/markdown in task prompts
        # reach fa verbatim (same reason the harbor adapter quotes).
        argv = [str(fah_bin), "--session-root", str(sessions), "-p", prompt]
        env, cap, _deadline = self._child_env(cfg)

        t0 = time.monotonic()
        outcome = "completed"
        with open(stdout_log, "wb") as tout, \
                open(stderr_log, "wb") as terr:
            proc = await asyncio.to_thread(
                subprocess.Popen,
                argv,
                stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
                stdout=tout,
                stderr=terr,
                env=env,
                cwd=str(wd),
                start_new_session=True,
            )
        pid_file.write_text(str(proc.pid), encoding="ascii")
        logger.info("fa deployer: spawned pid=%s (cap=%s)", proc.pid, cap)

        cancelled = False
        try:
            outcome = await self._watch(proc, wd, cfg, t0)
        except asyncio.CancelledError:
            cancelled = True
            outcome = "external_kill"
            _kill_process_group(proc, signal.SIGTERM)
            try:
                await asyncio.wait_for(
                    asyncio.to_thread(proc.wait), timeout=_TERM_GRACE_S
                )
            except (asyncio.TimeoutError, asyncio.CancelledError):
                _kill_process_group(proc, signal.SIGKILL)
                await asyncio.to_thread(proc.wait)
            raise
        finally:
            self._write_audit(wd, cfg, cap, outcome, proc, t0, cancelled)

        duration_s = time.monotonic() - t0
        exit_code = proc.returncode
        status = "completed" if exit_code == 0 else "failed"
        atif = await self._export_atif(fah_bin, sessions, wd)
        error = None
        if status == "failed":
            error = _tail(stderr_log) or _tail(stdout_log) or f"fa exited {exit_code}"
        return AgentRunResult(
            status=status,
            transcript_path=str(atif) if atif else None,
            stderr_path=str(stderr_log),
            pid=proc.pid,
            exit_code=exit_code,
            duration_s=duration_s,
            error=error,
        )

    async def _watch(
        self,
        proc: subprocess.Popen,
        wd: Path,
        cfg: FaConfig,
        t0: float,
    ) -> str:
        """Poll loop with the round-3 stall/ceiling watch.

        Progress = combined growth of the tee'd output streams (the same
        signal the harbor adapter's progress watch measures). Only
        declared knobs can kill — with no knobs this is a plain join and
        ALE's wall budget stays the authoritative kill.
        """
        stdout_log = wd / _STDOUT_FILENAME
        stderr_log = wd / _STDERR_FILENAME
        last_size = 0
        last_progress = time.monotonic()
        while proc.poll() is None:
            await asyncio.sleep(_POLL_INTERVAL_S)
            now = time.monotonic()
            size = _safe_size(stdout_log) + _safe_size(stderr_log)
            if size > last_size:
                last_size = size
                last_progress = now
            if cfg.abs_ceiling_sec is not None and now - t0 >= cfg.abs_ceiling_sec:
                logger.warning("fa deployer: abs ceiling %.0fs hit", cfg.abs_ceiling_sec)
                await self._reap(proc)
                return "agent_timeout"
            if cfg.stall_gap_sec is not None and now - last_progress >= cfg.stall_gap_sec:
                logger.warning(
                    "fa deployer: stall %.0fs (no output growth)", cfg.stall_gap_sec
                )
                await self._reap(proc)
                return "agent_timeout"
        return "completed" if proc.returncode == 0 else "failed"

    async def _reap(self, proc: subprocess.Popen) -> None:
        _kill_process_group(proc, signal.SIGTERM)
        try:
            await asyncio.wait_for(
                asyncio.to_thread(proc.wait), timeout=_TERM_GRACE_S
            )
        except (asyncio.TimeoutError, asyncio.CancelledError):
            _kill_process_group(proc, signal.SIGKILL)
            await asyncio.to_thread(proc.wait)

    async def _export_atif(
        self, fah_bin: Path, sessions: Path, wd: Path
    ) -> Path | None:
        """Best-effort `fa trajectory export --format atif`. Never raises;
        a missing export degrades to parse_artifacts' system note."""
        atif = wd / _ATIF_FILENAME
        cmd = [
            str(fah_bin),
            "--session-root",
            str(sessions),
            "trajectory",
            "export",
            "--format",
            "atif",
            "--output",
            str(atif),
        ]
        try:
            proc = await asyncio.to_thread(
                subprocess.Popen, cmd,
                stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
                stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
            )
            await asyncio.wait_for(
                asyncio.to_thread(proc.wait), timeout=_ATIF_EXPORT_TIMEOUT_S
            )
            if proc.returncode != 0:
                logger.warning(
                    "fa deployer: ATIF export exited %s: %s",
                    proc.returncode,
                    (proc.stderr.read() or b"")[-200:].decode(errors="replace"),
                )
        except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError, asyncio.TimeoutError) as exc:
            logger.warning("fa deployer: ATIF export failed: %s", exc)
        return atif if atif.exists() else None

    def _write_audit(
        self,
        wd: Path,
        cfg: FaConfig,
        cap: CapResolution | None,
        outcome: str,
        proc: subprocess.Popen,
        t0: float,
        cancelled: bool,
    ) -> None:
        """One audit record per trial: outcome class + the exact cap
        resolution that produced the deadline fa saw (AGENTS.md round-3
        audit contract; no env dumps — the key never lands here)."""
        audit: dict[str, Any] = {
            "outcome": outcome,
            "cancelled": cancelled,
            "exit_code": proc.returncode if proc.poll() is not None else None,
            "duration_s": round(time.monotonic() - t0, 2),
            "knobs": {
                "progress_extension": cfg.progress_extension,
                "stall_gap_sec": cfg.stall_gap_sec,
                "abs_ceiling_sec": cfg.abs_ceiling_sec,
                "external_cap_sec": cfg.external_cap_sec,
            },
            "cap_resolution": (
                {
                    "winning_cap_source": cap.winning_cap_source,
                    "effective_cap_sec": cap.effective_cap_sec,
                    "knob_cap_sec": cap.knob_cap_sec,
                    "external_cap_sec": cap.external_cap_sec,
                    "external_cap_status": cap.external_cap_status,
                }
                if cap is not None
                else None
            ),
        }
        (wd / _AUDIT_FILENAME).write_text(
            json.dumps(audit, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8"
        )

    # ──────────────────────────────────────────────── parse_artifacts ──

    @classmethod
    def parse_artifacts(
        cls,
        *,
        work_dir: Path,
        config: Any,
        run_result: AgentRunResult,
        builder: TrajectoryBuilder,
    ) -> None:
        """ATIF-v1.7 → TrajectoryBuilder. Pure; runs host-side on the
        gathered work_dir. Missing/cut-off export = one system note."""
        path = Path(work_dir) / _ATIF_FILENAME
        if not path.exists():
            builder.add_step(
                "system",
                message="no fa trajectory (ATIF export missing from work_dir)",
            )
            return
        try:

        for step in data.get("steps") or []:

        builder.override_final_metrics(
            total_input_tokens=final.get("total_prompt_tokens"),
            total_output_tokens=final.get("total_completion_tokens"),
            total_cache_read_tokens=final.get("total_cached_tokens"),
            total_cost_usd=final.get("total_cost_usd"),
        )


def atif_step_kwargs(step: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Map ONE ATIF step dict onto TrajectoryBuilder.add_step kwargs.

    Exported for tests (the fixture contract is cross-validated with
    bench/harbor_fa/test_atif_contract.py's atif_sample.json).
    """
    source = {"user": "user", "system": "system", "agent": "agent"}.get(
        step.get("source"), "system"
    )
    kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {"source": source}
    if step.get("message") is not None:
        kwargs["message"] = str(step["message"])
    if step.get("reasoning_content"):
        kwargs["reasoning"] = str(step["reasoning_content"])
    calls = []
    for call in step.get("tool_calls") or []:
        calls.append(
            ToolCall(
                id=str(call.get("tool_call_id", "")),
                name=str(call.get("function_name", "")),
                arguments=call.get("arguments") or {},
            )
        )
    if calls:
        kwargs["tool_calls"] = calls
    obs = step.get("observation")
    if obs:
        results = []
        for res in obs.get("results") or []:
            content = res.get("content")
            results.append(
                ToolResult(
                    tool_call_id=str(res.get("source_call_id", "")),
                    content=[
                        ContentPart(type="text", text=content)
                        if isinstance(content, str)
                        else ContentPart(type="text", text=json.dumps(content))
                    ],
                    is_error=bool(res.get("is_error", False)),
                )
            )
        kwargs["observation"] = Observation(results=results)
    metrics = step.get("metrics")
    if metrics:
        kwargs["metrics"] = StepMetrics(
            input_tokens=_int_or_none(metrics.get("prompt_tokens")),
            output_tokens=_int_or_none(metrics.get("completion_tokens")),
            cache_read_tokens=_int_or_none(metrics.get("cached_tokens")),
            cost_usd=_float_or_none(metrics.get("cost_usd")),
        )
    return kwargs


def _int_or_none(value: Any) -> int | None:
    try:
        return None if value is None else int(value)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None


def _float_or_none(value: Any) -> float | None:
    try:
        return None if value is None else float(value)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None


def _safe_size(path: Path) -> int:
    try:
        return path.stat().st_size
    except OSError:
        return 0


def _tail(path: Path, limit: int = 400) -> str | None:
    try:
        text = path.read_text(errors="replace")
    except OSError:
        return None
    return text[-limit:] or None

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""summary_ale.py — aggregate fa-on-ALE shard runs (issue #1686).

Input: one or more shard output roots (the ``.logs/ale-shard-<i>`` dirs
uploaded as per-shard artifacts). Each run unit lands as
``<root>/<agent_id>/<task...>/<variant>/<ts>/`` (RunWriter) with
``run.json`` + ``trajectory.json`` + ``eval_result.json`` + events.jsonl.

Outputs:
  * the markdown summary table + verdict on stdout (the workflow
    redirects into $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY),
  * ``--json-summary`` with the exact field names
    bench/leaderboard/record.py --summary consumes (family/model/
    resolved/total/date/fa_ref/run_url) so a complete full run can
    upsert the fa-results ledger (gh-1682 contract, self_reported).

Verdict rules (harbor summary parity):
  * a shard that contributed ZERO trials fails the run by name
    (gh-1658 C3),
  * coverage X/N over the expected task set; missing tasks listed.

resolved = eval_status == "success" and score >= 1.0 (ALE rewards are
graded in [0,1]; partial credit is not a resolution).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import sys
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

DEFAULT_FAMILY = "ALE-v1.1-docker"


def _load_json(path: Path) -> dict | None:
    try:
        return json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"))
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        return None


def collect_trials(roots: list[Path]) -> list[dict]:
    """Walk shard roots → one row per run unit (per attempt)."""
    rows: list[dict] = []
    for root in roots:
        shard = root.name
        for run_json in sorted(root.rglob("run.json")):
            run_dir = run_json.parent
            run_meta = _load_json(run_json)
            if run_meta is None:
                continue  # unparsable run dir — skipped, never fatal
            eval_meta = _load_json(run_dir / "eval_result.json") or {}
            traj_meta = _load_json(run_dir / "trajectory.json") or {}
            final = traj_meta.get("final_metrics") or {}
            agent_id = run_meta.get("agent_id") or _agent_from_path(run_dir, root)
            rows.append(
                {
                    "shard": shard,
                    "task": run_meta.get("task_path") or run_meta.get("task") or "?",
                    "agent_id": agent_id,
                    "status": run_meta.get("status"),
                    "eval_status": eval_meta.get("eval_status"),
                    "score": eval_meta.get("score", run_meta.get("score")),
                    "error": eval_meta.get("error") or run_meta.get("error"),
                    "duration_s": run_meta.get("total_duration_s"),
                    "steps": final.get("total_steps"),
                    "input_tokens": final.get("total_input_tokens"),
                    "output_tokens": final.get("total_output_tokens"),
                    "cost_usd": final.get("total_cost_usd"),
                }
            )
    return rows


def _agent_from_path(run_dir: Path, root: Path) -> str:
    rel = run_dir.relative_to(root)
    return rel.parts[0] if rel.parts else "?"


def resolved(row: dict) -> bool:
    return row.get("eval_status") == "success" and _score(row) >= 1.0


def _score(row: dict) -> float:
    try:
        return float(row.get("score") or 0.0)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return 0.0


def build_verdict(
    rows: list[dict],
    *,
    expected_tasks: int,
    expected_shards: int,
) -> tuple[bool, list[str]]:
    problems: list[str] = []
    shards_seen = sorted({row["shard"] for row in rows})
    counts: dict[str, int] = {shard: 0 for shard in shards_seen}
    for row in rows:
        counts[row["shard"]] = counts.get(row["shard"], 0) + 1
    if len(rows) == 0:
        problems.append("no trials found under the shard roots")
    else:
        empty = [s for s, n in counts.items() if n == 0]
        if empty:
            problems.append("shards with zero trials: " + ", ".join(empty))
    seen_tasks = {row["task"] for row in rows}
    if expected_tasks and len(rows) and len(seen_tasks) < expected_tasks:
        missing = expected_tasks - len(seen_tasks)
        problems.append(f"coverage {len(seen_tasks)}/{expected_tasks} ({missing} task(s) produced no run dir)")
    if expected_shards and len(rows) and len(shards_seen) < expected_shards:
        problems.append(f"only {len(shards_seen)}/{expected_shards} shards contributed artifacts")
    return (not problems), problems


def render_markdown(
    rows: list[dict],
    *,
    ok: bool,
    problems: list[str],
    model: str,
    run_label: str,
) -> str:
    lines = [
        f"## fa on Agents' Last Exam — {run_label}",
        "",
        f"Model: `{model}` · trials: {len(rows)} · "
        f"resolved: {sum(1 for r in rows if resolved(r))}",
        "",
        "| task | status | eval | score | dur (s) | steps | in/out tok |",
        "|---|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|",
    ]
    for row in rows:
        score = "-" if row.get("score") is None else f"{_score(row):.2f}"
        lines.append(
            "| {task} | {status} | {eval_status} | {score} | {dur} | {steps} | {tok} |".format(
                task=str(row.get("task", "?"))[:80],
                status=row.get("status") or "?",
                eval_status=row.get("eval_status") or "?",
                score=score,
                dur=row.get("duration_s") if row.get("duration_s") is not None else "-",
                steps=row.get("steps") if row.get("steps") is not None else "-",
                tok=(
                    f"{row.get('input_tokens') or 0}/{row.get('output_tokens') or 0}"
                ),
            )
        )
    lines.append("")
    if ok:
        lines.append("verdict: PASS — all expected shards contributed; coverage complete")
    else:
        lines.append("verdict: FAIL")
        for problem in problems:
            lines.append(f"- {problem}")
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def json_summary(
    rows: list[dict],
    *,
    model: str,
    fa_ref: str,
    run_url: str,
    family: str,
) -> dict:
    """Exact consumer contract: bench/leaderboard/record.py --summary
    requires family/model/resolved/total/date (+fa_ref/run_url optional
    but expected)."""
    tasks = {row["task"]: row for row in rows}
    resolved_count = sum(1 for row in tasks.values() if resolved(row))
    return {
        "family": family,
        "model": model,
        "resolved": resolved_count,
        "total": len(tasks),
        "date": datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%d"),
        "fa_ref": fa_ref,
        "run_url": run_url,
    }


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("roots", nargs="+", type=Path, help="shard output roots")
    parser.add_argument("--expected-tasks", type=int, default=0)
    parser.add_argument("--expected-shards", type=int, default=0)
    parser.add_argument("--model", default="glm-5.3-flash")
    parser.add_argument("--run-label", default="ALE-V1")
    parser.add_argument("--fa-ref", default="")
    parser.add_argument("--run-url", default="")
    parser.add_argument("--family", default=DEFAULT_FAMILY)
    parser.add_argument(
        "--json-summary",
        dest="json_summary",
        default=None,
        help="write the record.py-compatible totals JSON here",
    )
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    rows = collect_trials(args.roots)
    ok, problems = build_verdict(
        rows,
        expected_tasks=args.expected_tasks,
        expected_shards=args.expected_shards,
    )
    sys.stdout.write(
        render_markdown(
            rows, ok=ok, problems=problems, model=args.model, run_label=args.run_label
        )
    )
    if args.json_summary:
        Path(args.json_summary).write_text(
            json.dumps(
                json_summary(
                    rows,
                    model=args.model,
                    fa_ref=args.fa_ref,
                    run_url=args.run_url,
                    family=args.family,
                ),
                indent=2,
            )
            + "\n",
            encoding="utf-8",
        )
    return 0 if ok else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

def _write_run(root: Path, task: str, variant: int, ts: str, *, status="completed",
               eval_status="success", score=1.0, steps=12, in_tok=1000, out_tok=50):
    run_dir = root / "fa" / task / str(variant) / ts

        "task_path": task, "agent_id": "fa", "status": status,

    }))
    (run_dir / "eval_result.json").write_text(json.dumps({
        "eval_status": eval_status, "score": score,
        "eval_duration_s": 5.0, "error": None,
    }))
